sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The window is not a smooth compounder: revenue grew 0.3% in FY2019 and fell 1.1% in FY2020, then jumped 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D97][D143][D280][D421].
The FY2023 step change came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year's total [S61][D604][P48].
FY2026's 17.3% growth was driven by cloud revenues, with cloud infrastructure contributing 84% of the constant-currency cloud growth [D421][P17].
Cloud Infrastructure is now the growth engine: revenue of $18.1 billion, 26.9% of the total, added 13.7pp of FY2026 growth [S92][D643][D645].
Cloud Applications grew 11.3% to $15.9 billion and added 2.8pp, while Software License fell 8.9% and subtracted 0.8pp [S101][D667][D668][S107][D681][D682].
The filing attributes the cloud and software revenue increase to customers purchasing applications and infrastructure technologies and renewing cloud contracts [P17].
Operating income grew 16.6% against revenue growth of 17.3%, so incremental operating margin was 29.4%, well below the 30.6% operating margin itself [D422][D421][D442][F34].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against net income growth of 36.5%, with the diluted share count up 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin of 30.6% sits below the window median of 32.2% and far below the FY2021 high of 37.6%, but above the FY2022 low of 25.7% [F34][D788][D787][D786].
FY2026 operating margin slipped 0.2pp as operating expenses grew 17.7% against revenue growth of 17.3% [D433][D436][D421].
The expense increase was led by a $6.0 billion rise in cloud and software expenses from higher infrastructure spending and a $1.5 billion rise in restructuring [P19].
The cloud and software segment margin fell to 58.9% from 62.8% because infrastructure expenses to support cloud infrastructure growth rose [D761][D760][P16].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4% from 39.2%, helped by $1.5 billion more in stock-based compensation tax benefits [D434][F54][D407][D360][P9].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion, 47.5% of revenue, but free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin [D426][F84][D406][F104][D405].
Capex of $55.7 billion, 82.6% of revenue, drove the free-cash-flow deficit, up $34.4 billion year over year [F94][D404][P5].
Free cash flow covered -1.39x of net income against a window median of 1.06x, and capex ran at 7.30x D&A [D409][D800][D410].
Operating cash flow benefited from higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion, 145.0% of revenue, against a software peer median of -0.5% net cash, the 0th percentile of six peers [D414][D415][D816][D815].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $5.9 billion were 25% of the negative free cash flow, and the diluted share count rose 1.7% after years of shrinkage [D416][F104][D438].
The company also raised $5.0 billion of mandatory convertible preferred stock and cut buybacks to $95 million [P7][X155].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the latest burn, the most severe flag [D412][D419][R1].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for two years, at -0.03x in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026 [D362][D409][R2].
Net cash has fallen into deeper net debt for two straight years, from -$76.2 billion in FY2024 to -$97.6 billion in FY2026 [D320][D367][D414][R3].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure of $17.1 billion by up to 0.60% [F44][X20][R5].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 26.0% window median from -35.2%, which requires capex to fall below the FY2026 level of $55.7 billion [D794][D405][F94].
Whether net debt stays above the FY2026 level of $97.6 billion or reverses, given $260 billion of additional data-center lease commitments not yet on balance sheet [D414][P1].
Whether Cloud Infrastructure growth holds near the FY2026 rate of 76.9%, since it supplied 13.7pp of total growth [D644][D645].
